questions.question: Why does a Map handle object keys better than a plain object? When would you still choose a plain object?
questions.answer:
A plain object coerces every non-symbol key to a string, so two different objects both become "[object Object]" and the second write overwrites the first. A Map stores the actual key value and compares keys with SameValueZero: objects by reference, NaN equal to NaN. It also has a real size, is directly iterable in insertion order, and does not inherit keys from Object.prototype.

You still choose an object for a fixed record shape you know in advance (user.name, config.port), for JSON payloads, for destructuring, and for methods. Choose a Map when keys arrive at runtime, are objects or numbers, when entries are frequently added and deleted, or when guaranteed insertion order and a cheap size matter.
key_points: Object keys are strings or symbols only; objects stringify to "[object Object]"
Map keys can be any value and are compared by reference for objects
Map has size, iteration, and no prototype keys
Use objects for fixed records and JSON, Maps for dynamic keyed data

questions.question: What can a WeakMap do that a Map cannot, and what does it give up in return?
questions.answer:
A WeakMap holds its object keys weakly, so an entry does not keep the key alive. When nothing else references the key object, the garbage collector may remove the entry and its value. That makes WeakMap ideal for metadata attached to objects, private state, and caches keyed by object, because the cache cannot cause a leak.

In return it gives up almost every convenience: keys must be objects (or non-registered symbols), there is no size, no clear, no iteration, and no way to list keys. Those restrictions exist so the engine can collect entries safely. Map is the right choice when you need to count, iterate, serialise, or use primitive keys; WeakMap is only for hidden per-object data.
key_points: Weak keys do not prevent garbage collection
Object keys only; no size, clear, or iteration
Best for metadata, private state, and object-keyed caches
Use Map when you need enumeration or primitive keys

questions.answer:
It prints 2 undefined, then 1 b.

key1 and key2 are two different objects. Map compares object keys by reference with SameValueZero, so both entries exist and size is 2. The freshly created { id: 1 } in m.get(...) is a third reference, so the lookup misses and returns undefined.

The plain object stringifies both keys to "[object Object]". The second assignment overwrites the first, leaving one own key whose value is "b". This is exactly the collision a Map avoids. To look up by shape you must keep the original reference, or key the collection by a primitive such as id.
key_points: Map object keys are compared by reference
A new object literal never matches a stored object key
Object keys stringify, so objects collide on "[object Object]"
Key by id when you need shape-based lookup

questions.answer:
It prints 5, then a 1, then 1 undefined.

The Set contains 1, "1", NaN, and two distinct object references: 1 and "1" are different types, the duplicate NaN collapses because SameValueZero treats NaN as equal to itself, but the two { id: 1 } objects are different references and both stay. So size is 5, not 3.

Map.prototype.forEach calls its callback with (value, key, map), the reverse of Array.prototype.forEach's (element, index, array). The entry "a" -> 1 therefore logs "a 1". A Map has size, not length, so m.length is undefined.
key_points: Set uses SameValueZero: NaN dedupes, 1 and "1" differ
Objects dedupe only by reference
Map forEach callback is (value, key, map)
Use map.size, not map.length

questions.answer:
It prints undefined, then TypeError, then {}.

A WeakMap deliberately exposes no size, no keys, and no iterator, so cache.size is undefined and spreading it throws TypeError: cache is not iterable. The same restrictions let the garbage collector remove entries whose keys are no longer referenced. You can only check a key you already hold with cache.has(key) or cache.get(key).

JSON.stringify does not know about Map or Set internals, so a Map becomes an empty object. Convert first with Object.fromEntries(map) or [...map], and for a Set use [...set]. A WeakMap cannot be serialised at all, by design.
key_points: WeakMap has no size, iteration, or clear
Spreading a WeakMap throws TypeError
JSON.stringify(new Map()) is "{}"
Convert with Object.fromEntries or spread for Map/Set
